description: Two-panel composite figure reporting the mechanical properties of the Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C low-density test steel after cryogenic rolling (CR). (a) is a set of engineering stress–strain curves (x-axis "Engineering strain (%)", 0–70; y-axis "Engineering stress (MPa)", 0–2000) with five colour-coded curves listed in the legend: Undeformed, CR 30%, CR 50%, CR 70% and CR 90%. The Undeformed curve is the lowest and most ductile, peaking between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines at roughly 60% strain; as the CR reduction rises the curves shift up and to the left — higher peak stress at progressively smaller strain — with the CR 90% curve peaking between the 1800 and 1900 MPa gridlines below about 5% strain. (b) is a multi-axis summary plot versus "Deformation/%" at 0, 30, 50, 70 and 90, with a left "Strength/Mpa" axis and two right axes, red "Elongation/%" (0–80) and blue "Microhardness/HV" (700–300 top-down): tensile strength (squares), yield strength (circles), elongation (red triangles) and microhardness (stars). All four properties carry printed data labels. Together the panels demonstrate a pronounced strength–ductility trade-off under CR.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress–strain curves for five conditions (Undeformed, CR 30%, CR 50%, CR 70%, CR 90%) plotted over Engineering strain 0–70% and Engineering stress 0–2000 MPa. The Undeformed curve reaches the lowest peak stress and the largest strain to failure; increasing CR reduction raises the peak stress and shortens the curve, with CR 90% giving the highest peak stress at the smallest strain. No data labels are printed on the curves.

Multi-axis property summary versus Deformation/% (0, 30, 50, 70, 90) with Strength/Mpa on the left axis and Elongation/% (red, 0–80) plus Microhardness/HV (blue) on the right. Printed values: tensile strength 882, 1261, 1518, 1693, 1861 MPa; yield strength 505, 1092, 1379, 1588, 1791 MPa; elongation 64.5, 13.6, 8.8, 7.2, 6.6 %; microhardness 284, 435, 479, 530, 578 HV.

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend lists exactly five conditions: Undeformed, CR 30%, CR 50%, CR 70% and CR 90%, colour-coded as black, red, blue, green and purple respectively.
Panel (a) x-axis is labelled "Engineering strain (%)" ranging 0–70 and the y-axis is labelled "Engineering stress (MPa)" ranging 0–2000, with gridlines every 200 MPa and every 10% strain.
The Undeformed curve has the lowest peak stress (plateau between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines) and the largest strain to failure (drops to zero shortly after 60% strain).
Peak stress increases and fracture strain decreases monotonically from CR 30% through CR 90%; the CR 90% curve peaks between the 1800 and 1900 MPa gridlines at a strain below 5%.
Panel (b) plots four properties against Deformation/% (0, 30, 50, 70, 90) using a left axis labelled "Strength/Mpa" and two right axes labelled "Elongation/%" (red) and "Microhardness/HV" (blue).
Tensile strength data labels in panel (b) read 882, 1261, 1518, 1693 and 1861 MPa for 0, 30, 50, 70 and 90% deformation.
Yield strength data labels in panel (b) read 505, 1092, 1379, 1588 and 1791 MPa for 0, 30, 50, 70 and 90% deformation.
Elongation data labels in panel (b) read 64.5, 13.6, 8.8, 7.2 and 6.6 % for 0, 30, 50, 70 and 90% deformation, showing a steep fall from the undeformed state to 90% CR.
Microhardness data labels in panel (b) read 284, 435, 479, 530 and 578 HV for 0, 30, 50, 70 and 90% deformation.
The caption states that panel (a) is an engineering stress–strain curve and panel (b) reports UTS, YS, elongation and microhardness.
The citing text states the initial steel has UTS and YS of 882 and 505 MPa, microhardness 284 HV and elongation of 64%, matching the printed labels in panel (b).

The citing text states the highest UTS, YS and microhardness of 1.86, 1.79 GPa and 578 HV are obtained at 90% CR reduction, i.e. increments of 111%, 255% and 104% relative to the initial state, while elongation falls to barely 6.6%.
The citing text interprets the trend as a clear strength–ductility trade-off caused by enhanced work hardening and grain-boundary strengthening during cryogenic rolling.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the curves carry no printed data labels, so exact peak stresses and fracture strains must be inferred from the (b) tabulated values; the peak positions are only readable relative to the gridlines
panel (b): small error bars are visible on the microhardness and elongation points but their magnitudes cannot be read reliably at the supplied resolution
